name: Sequences and Attention
strandNote: Not needed for the quant path. Machine learning research roles, and reading transformer papers.
description: Train a recurrent net through time, then build attention, self-attention and a transformer block in NumPy.

skills.sqn-rnn: Recurrent networks and backprop through time

requires.why: A linear RNN is the AR(1) recursion of l2, with a weight to learn.
A shock fading as phi to the k, from l7, is the gradient through time; a quick check helps.
Gradients through time explode or vanish by the eigenvalues of repeated multiplication, from l4.
Vanishing gradients and initialisation were taught there; this level meets them through time.
Attention is the nearest-neighbour average of l4 with softmax weights instead of a hard k.
A causal model is scored by held-out loss per character on names, as there.
The residual block of l11 is the first identity path; a quick check helps.

lessonNames.l8-scaled-dot-product: Why divide by the square root of d

lessonObjectives.l1-memory-in-a-loop: Write a linear recurrent net and match it to an AR(1), then add a tanh.
lessonObjectives.l2-unrolling: Unroll a recurrent net and compute its gradient through time with the array autograd.
lessonObjectives.l3-exploding-and-vanishing: Explain from the eigenvalues of the recurrent weight why gradients through time explode or vanish.
lessonObjectives.l4-clipping-and-gates: Write gradient clipping by norm, and explain how a gate lets a gradient survive many steps.
lessonObjectives.l5-lookup-table: Look up a value by matching a query to keys, and see why a hard lookup has no gradient.
lessonObjectives.l6-soft-neighbours: Build a softmax-weighted average of neighbours, and set its temperature on held-out error.
lessonObjectives.l7-queries-keys-values: Write attention with query, key and value matrices, and check its shapes.
lessonObjectives.l8-scaled-dot-product: Derive why scores are divided by the square root of the key size, and see softmax saturate without it.
lessonObjectives.l9-self-attention: Write self-attention over a sequence, and read its attention matrix.
lessonObjectives.l10-causal-mask: Build a causal mask, and test that no position can see a later one.
lessonObjectives.l11-many-heads: Write multi-head attention by splitting and joining the model width.
lessonObjectives.l12-positions: Explain why attention needs positions, and add learned or sinusoidal position vectors.
lessonObjectives.l13-the-block: Build a pre-norm transformer block from attention, a feed-forward net and layer normalisation.
lessonObjectives.l14-residual-stream: Explain the residual stream as a sum that every layer reads from and writes to.
lessonObjectives.l15-counting-a-block: Count the parameters of a transformer block and of a one-block model, and check the count in code.
lessonObjectives.l16-a-tiny-transformer: Run a two-block transformer from supplied weights, and train it for a few steps on a toy task.
